knowledge_answers.rationale: The ball becomes dead and five Penalty runs are awarded to the batting side when it strikes the fielding side's helmet on the ground, subject to listed restrictions.
No ball overrides Wide; the Wide call is revoked.
Wide bars Bowled, Caught, Hit the ball twice and LBW; Hit wicket, Obstructing the field, Run out and Stumped remain available.

The Dead-ball state takes effect at the governing incident or call; a Run out or other live-ball dismissal requires the ball to be in play; the later broken wicket therefore cannot create the dismissal.
A completed Run out makes the ball dead at the wicket; completed runs before the wicket was fairly broken stand; the later rope contact occurs after Dead ball and adds no boundary.
